evidence: Cic. Fam. 15.17.3: exspectātiō valdē magna (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With adjectives, adverbs and verbs. Latin’s commonest “very”, though, is no separate word: the superlative (facillimē, very easily: Cic. Fam. 9.24.3) or per- on the adjective or adverb (perbellē, very nicely: Cic. Att. 4.4a.1).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 10: nōn admodum grandem nātū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Often after its word (paucī admodum); nōn admodum, not very.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.201: perquam breviter (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 7.27.1: perquam velim scīre (Lewis & Short)

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: confined to familiar talk, and already old-fashioned in Quintilian’s day (Quint. 8.3.25).
